scope: fourth external corpus (21 third-party LICENSE files); defects 14 and 15; the 27th catalog entry

corpus.type: LICENSE files from 21 plugin repositories pulled for the catalog research
remainingTwoAreReal: ECNU__EduWork/LICENSE — the body is not a recognised license (self-written or a template)
op7418__dsh-guizang-design/LICENSE — titled MIT, body is AGPL-3.0

defects.bug: the rule took the first line containing 'copyright', which in Apache-2.0 is the definitions section: "Licensor" shall mean the copyright owner…
defects.impact: four correct third-party LICENSE files reported as missing both a year and a holder
defects.fix: a notice has a shape — the word or (c) immediately followed by (c), a four-digit year, or a bracket slot

defects.bug: severity did not depend on the license: MIT, BSD and ISC expect the notice filled in, while Apache-2.0, MPL-2.0 and the GPL family ship the appendix as a template to copy elsewhere and most correct projects leave it alone
defects.impact: an unfilled Apache appendix produced two errors on files that were fine
defects.fix: severity follows the license: notice-expected => error; recognised-but-template => one warning (notice-template-unfilled); unrecognised body => error

selfCorrection: the first attempt at defect 15 demoted every appendix slot, which broke the MIT case (a missing year there is a real defect). The legacy test caught it. The mapping is by license, not by the shape of the line.
gateCaughtMe: the rules audit flagged notice-template-unfilled as silent-only ten minutes after I added it — the new rule had no firing test until the audit demanded one
